stem: A breeder selects one unusually vigorous plant from a variable population after a single grow. Why is it premature to conclude that the vigor is stably inherited?
choices: One phenotype does not separate inherited effects from environmental effects or demonstrate progeny consistency
Any selected phenotype becomes genetically fixed immediately
Vigor cannot have a genetic component
Selection has no relationship to breeding outcomes
rationale: A single observed phenotype does not by itself establish genetic stability or heritability. Replication, environmental context, and progeny evidence help separate inherited effects from environmental influence.
